status: declared by the pull request that closes #941 before any score was computed; a development study, never a verdict. Nothing is published: no variant joins any published declaration, `gbm_funding`'s declaration and `scripts/final_test_preregistration.py` do not change, no day after 2025-12-31 is scored, no lockbox day is scored, and no record in docs/runs/ is edited. Any change to the candidate is Eleonora's decision. Amendments made after a number was computed would be listed in `amendments` and named as such; there are none.
avenue: #836 (filtered historical simulation); the ruling of 19 October 2026 on #941 and its comment 6273987279
hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3, calibration of the predictive law, in particular the upper tail. Development tier
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)

base.name: spread_mr_level10 (#686), unscaled
base.formula: q_p(t+h) = level + phi^k * (last - level) + eps_h,p. level, k, phi, the two-year training window, the minimum of 60 pairs and the refit every 21 decision days are as in metadata/spread_distribution_686.json. Each variant reuses the base fit's phi, level and anchor and changes only the residual pool, as this file says

scale.definition: scale(r) at panel row r = max(floor, 1.4826 * median(|s_j - s_(j-1)|, j = r - window + 1 .. r)), where s is the panel's spread_bps. It reads rows r - window .. r and no row after r
scale.named_estimator: median absolute daily spread change (MAD of the changes about zero), times 1.4826
scale.sensitivity_estimator: the sample standard deviation (n - 1) of the same window of changes, in place of 1.4826 * median(|change|), with the same floor. It is the one named sensitivity: #836 found that the 2018-19 CRPS depends on the estimator
scale.as_of: the scale at the anchor is read from rows at or before the anchor, the last row public at the decision instant (protocol_benchmarks._anchor runs both guards of the information-set rule); every row the scale reads is required public (protocol_benchmarks._require_public raises LookAheadError otherwise). No regime label and no other column is an input

fit.pool: for lead h, each training pair (origin o, target s, k rows apart) has the raw residual (spread[s] - level[o]) - phi^k * (spread[o] - level[o]), exactly as the base model forms it. It is divided by scale(o), the scale at its own origin; a pair whose origin has no scale (fewer than window + 1 rows) is left out. The 23 empirical quantiles of the standardised pool are kept (protocol_benchmarks.empirical_quantiles)
fit.forecast: level + phi^k * (last - level) + scale(anchor) * (the standardised pool's quantile), level by level; the order of the quantiles is kept, so no crossing
fit.phi: the base fit's, on all pairs: no new parameter
fit.refit: every 21 decision days, with the base fit; between refits the standardised pool is kept and last, level, k, the anchor and scale(anchor) are read afresh

listed_in_full.name: spread_mr_fhs_sd20_f0.5
listed_in_full.role: the one named sensitivity: the standard deviation

variants.no_others: no variant is added after a number is computed; the grid is a cross of one parameter at a time around the declared variant, not a full product

references.unscaled: spread_mr_level10 (#686): the base model, whose forecasts the walk reproduces exactly as spread_mean_reversion.walk does
references.benchmarks: B1 and B2 of scoring protocol v1 (repo_model.protocol_benchmarks)
references.current_law: gbm_funding (#634), walked per lead by scripts/spread_distribution_634.py walk, read only for the hit sequences below, and only when its walks are supplied; its declaration does not change

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.days: decision days with a forecast of every model, whose five targets (h = 1..5 business days on the panel's calendar) fall on or before 2025-12-31; no day after 2025-12-31 is read; the scored days pass lockbox.require_unlocked
scoring.outcomes: the panel's spread_bps at the target day, not the first-published vintage of protocol section 11
scoring.paired: each variant against unscaled mean reversion, B1 and B2: skill = mean(d) / mean(S(benchmark)) with d = S(benchmark) - S(candidate), positive favours the candidate; scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 941; two-sided 90% interval. A comparison the studentization cannot resolve is reported as undefined, with the means
measures: grid CRPS (23 levels), by lead and the mean over leads 1..5
upper-tail twCRPS, weight 1{z > 0 bp}, by lead and the mean over leads

exceedance calibration at +0, +5 and +10 bp: P(spread > tau) read off the 23 quantiles (repo_model.spread_mean_reversion.exceedance), the event on whole basis points strictly above tau (data.exceeds_bp); the Brier score paired like the CRPS, and the reliability slope and intercept of the logistic fit of the event on logit(p) (repo_model.reliability_regimes.fit; 1 and 0 for a reliable forecast) with a 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval and its difference from unscaled mean reversion on the same resamples

90% interval coverage (q05 to q95) and 50% interval coverage (q25 to q75): the share of cells whose outcome is inside, closed at both ends, with the same interval and its difference from unscaled mean reversion

splits.pooled: one number per decision day (protocol section 3); the calibration measures are read on the cells (decision day, lead)
splits.by_lead: h = 1..5, one number per decision day at that lead
splits.regime: SplitDeclaration.regime of the target day (metadata/evaluation_splits.json): 2018-19, 2020, 2021-23, 2024, 2025-26; 2021-23 is called out
splits.pressure_day_type: SplitDeclaration.reporting_day_type of the target day: quarter_end, month_end, tax_date, ordinary; quarter-ends and ordinary days are called out
splits.unit: every split is on the target day: a target day's score is the mean over the leads that forecast it, and it belongs to the group of its own date; a group's days are tested as a subsequence, as in #761
splits.min_days: a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested

hit_sequences.ruling: Eleonora, 19 October 2026, comment 6273987279 on #941: a by-lead hit sequence for gbm_funding's q90, q95 and q99, with three tests (Kupiec unconditional coverage, Christoffersen independence, Christoffersen conditional coverage), for the current law and for each recalibration variant
hit_sequences.sequence: for lead h, the decision days in order, with hit = 1 when the outcome at day d + h is beyond the model's quantile at the level in its law for d + h. One sequence per model, level and lead
hit_sequences.tests: repo_model.coverage_tests: kupiec, christoffersen_independence, christoffersen_conditional_coverage (#993). Reporting only: nothing here sets a gate
hit_sequences.hit_rule: OPEN QUESTION, Eleonora's (#993, coverage_tests.hit_sequence takes the rule as a required argument): 'beyond' is y > q or y >= q, and whole-bp targets tie with a quantile. This study reports both rules, side by side, and chooses neither
hit_sequences.days: when gbm_funding's walks are supplied, every model is read on the decision days on which gbm_funding has a law at that lead, so the rows compare like with like; otherwise on the scored days. Pooled for all three tests; within a regime for all three (a regime is a run of consecutive days); within a pressure-day type for the Kupiec test only (the days of a type are not consecutive, so the independence tests are not read there)
hit_sequences.models: gbm_funding when its walks are supplied, unscaled mean reversion, each variant, B1 and B2

rules: A variant's gain over unscaled mean reversion is read as present on a split when the 90% interval of its grid-CRPS skill over unscaled mean reversion excludes zero on the positive side, and as a loss when it excludes zero on the negative side; otherwise as undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the regime and pressure-day-type splits beside it; a gain pooled and a loss in 2018-19, 2021-23 or on quarter-end days is reported as mixed.
The standard deviation variant is read against the median-absolute-change variant of the same window and floor, as the one named sensitivity of the estimator.

A calibration measure moving toward its nominal value (slope toward 1, coverage toward 0.90 and 0.50, hit rate toward 1 - level) is reported with its interval; a hit-sequence p-value is reported as a p-value and is no gate.
Nothing in this study is a verdict, and the page says so. Whether any variant joins a candidate is Eleonora's decision.

questions: The hit rule ('above' or 'at or above') for the hit sequences is open and is Eleonora's; both are reported.
The 2026 development days (#684) are not read here.
